settings.name: JPEG/HEIF Switch
settings.display_rule: With the switch on movie or S&Q the row shows JPEG whatever is stored (the switch applies to stills).
settings.help: Whether processed pictures are saved as JPEG or HEIF; HEIF keeps more quality in a smaller file, but not every program opens it.
option_help: HEIF with less colour detail and smaller files.
HEIF keeping more colour detail, for editing.

settings.name: File Format (one slot)
settings.note: File Format for single-slot recording: RAW 0, RAW & JPEG 1, RAW & HEIF 2, JPEG 3, HEIF 4. The list shows RAW, RAW & JPEG, JPEG with JPEG/HEIF Switch on JPEG, and RAW, RAW & HEIF, HEIF with it on HEIF; the switch writes HEIF 4 here from JPEG. With Recording Media on one slot, Image Quality Settings has one column.
settings.display_rule: With the switch on movie or S&Q the row shows JPEG whatever is stored (the switch applies to stills).
settings.help: Which files a still is saved as: RAW, JPEG or HEIF, or RAW together with one of them.

settings.name: Aspect Ratio
settings.help: The shape of still pictures: 3:2 uses the whole sensor, the others crop it.

settings.name: Movie File Format
settings.help: The format movies are recorded in: XAVC HS (H.265), XAVC S (H.264) or XAVC S-I (intra-frame), at 8K, 4K or HD.
option_help: H.265 at 8K: high quality in small files.
H.265 at 4K: high quality in small files.
H.264 at 4K, which more devices and programs play.
H.264 at HD (1080), which more devices and programs play.
Intra-frame at 4K: large files that are the easiest to edit.
Intra-frame at HD (1080): large files that are the easiest to edit.

settings.name: APS-C/Super 35mm
settings.help: Records only the centre of the sensor, the APS-C / Super 35mm area, as a smaller camera would.
option_help: Switches to the APS-C / Super 35mm area when an APS-C lens is attached.

settings.name: Long Exposure NR
settings.help: After exposures of about a second or longer, takes a dark exposure of the same length to remove noise; you wait that long before the next shot.

settings.name: High ISO NR
settings.help: Reduces noise in JPEG and HEIF pictures taken at high ISO; RAW files are not affected.

settings.name: HLG Still Image
settings.help: Records HEIF stills with an HLG tone curve, for viewing on HDR screens.

settings.name: Color Space
settings.help: sRGB suits screens and most printing; AdobeRGB holds a wider range of colours for print work, where your software handles it.

settings.name: Shooting family (stills / movie / S&Q / time-lapse)
settings.note: Stills 0, Movie 1, S&Q Motion 2, Time-lapse 3. Follows the still/movie/S&Q switch (the camera writes the switch position here on load), or the Shoot Mode carousel with Mode Dial Control Set = Set with Menu. View only.

settings.name: Shooting family (stills / movie / time-lapse)
settings.note: S&Q Motion and Time-lapse both 2. Follows the still/movie/S&Q switch (the camera writes the switch position here on load), or the Shoot Mode carousel with Mode Dial Control Set = Set with Menu. View only.

settings.name: Memory/Recall Media
settings.help: Which card the memories kept on a memory card are saved to and recalled from.

settings.name: Drive Mode
settings.help: How pictures are taken when you press the shutter button: one at a time, in a burst, after a self-timer, or as a bracket of pictures that differ in exposure, focus, white balance or D-Range Optimizer.
option_help: Takes several pictures after the self-timer runs out.
Takes the bracketed exposures in one burst while you hold the button.
Takes one picture of the bracket with each press.
Takes a series with the focus moved step by step, for focus stacking.
Takes three pictures with differing white balance from one press.
Takes three pictures with differing D-Range Optimizer levels from one press.

settings.name: Drive Mode (menu choice)
settings.note: Takes the same codes as Drive Mode 0x02b5 when the drive mode is chosen from the menu, on a body Camera Settings Reset has set 0x1126 to 7 on, which a file cannot set back: a body never reset may not keep this record in step. A settings file sets it.

settings.name: Drive Mode
settings.help: How pictures are taken when you press the shutter button: one at a time, in a burst, after a self-timer, or as a bracket of pictures that differ in exposure, focus, white balance or D-Range Optimizer.
option_help: Takes several pictures after the self-timer runs out.
Takes the bracketed exposures in one burst while you hold the button.
Takes one picture of the bracket with each press.
Takes a series with the focus moved step by step, for focus stacking.
Takes three pictures with differing white balance from one press.
Takes three pictures with differing D-Range Optimizer levels from one press.

settings.help: Whether Cont. Bracket is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Continuous Shooting: Hi
settings.help: Whether Continuous Shooting: Hi is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Continuous Shooting: Hi+
settings.help: Whether Continuous Shooting: Hi+ is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Continuous Shooting: Lo

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Continuous Shooting: Mid

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: DRO Bracket
settings.help: Whether DRO Bracket is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Focus Bracket
settings.help: Whether Focus Bracket is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Self-timer (Cont)
settings.help: Whether Self-timer (Cont) is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Self-timer (Single)
settings.help: Whether Self-timer (Single) is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Single Bracket
settings.help: Whether Single Bracket is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: Single Shooting
settings.help: Whether Single Shooting is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Drive Mode Limit: WB Bracket
settings.help: Whether WB Bracket is offered when you change Drive Mode.

settings.name: Cnt Sht Spd Bst Settings
settings.help: The faster burst rate continuous shooting switches to while you hold the key assigned to Speed Boost.

settings.name: Self-timer Type
settings.note: Self-timer Type: Single or Cont.
settings.display_rule: The row follows the drive mode in use, not the stored type, until a self-timer drive mode is selected.
settings.help: Whether the self-timer takes one picture or several.

settings.name: Pixel Shift Multi Shoot.
settings.help: Takes 4 or 16 RAW pictures while moving the sensor a tiny step between them, to be combined on a computer into one picture with more detail; for still subjects on a tripod.

settings.name: Shutter Type
settings.help: Which shutter takes stills: the mechanical one, the electronic one, or the camera's choice.
option_help: The camera picks the shutter to suit the conditions.
Silent and free of vibration.

settings.name: Release w/o Lens
settings.help: Lets the shutter fire with no lens attached, for adapters and lenses that do not talk to the camera.

settings.name: Release w/o Card
settings.help: Lets the shutter fire with no card inserted; the pictures are not saved.

settings.name: SteadyShot
settings.help: Reduces blur from camera shake by moving the sensor.

settings.name: SteadyShot (Movie)
settings.help: How strongly movies are stabilised: Active and Dynamic active steady handheld walking shots more, but crop the frame a little.

settings.name: SteadyShot Adjust
settings.help: Auto takes the focal length from the lens; Manual uses the SteadyShot Focal Length you set, for lenses that cannot report it.

settings.name: Grid Line Display
settings.help: Shows grid lines on the shooting screen to help with composition.

settings.name: Grid Line Type
settings.help: The pattern of the grid lines.

settings.name: Aspect Marker
settings.help: Shows lines on the shooting screen for another picture shape, to frame for a later crop.

settings.name: Aspect Marker Type
settings.help: The picture shape the aspect marker lines show.

settings.name: Silent Mode Aperture Drive In AF
settings.help: What Silent Mode sets Aperture Drive In AF to, or Not Target to leave it as it is.

settings.name: Silent Mode target: Auto Pixel Mapping
settings.note: Silent Mode Settings > Target Function Settings > Auto Pixel Mapping: whether Silent Mode turns Auto Pixel Mapping off.
settings.help: Whether Silent Mode turns Auto Pixel Mapping off.

settings.name: File Name (prefix)
settings.note: Text: the 3-character file-name prefix as ASCII bytes, the first in the low byte (DSC = 0x435344; typed DSD = 0x445344). Stills' File/Folder Settings > Set File Name.
settings.help: The three letters each still's file name starts with.

settings.name: Title Name
settings.note: Text: the movie title, one ASCII byte per character, zero-filled ("C" read 67, 0...; typed "Ca" read 67, 97, 0...).
settings.help: The title used in movie file names when File Name Format includes a title.

settings.name: Exposure mode (P/A/S/M)
settings.note: The exposure mode in use: follows the mode dial (the camera writes the dial position here on load), or the Shoot Mode carousel with Mode Dial Control Set = Set with Menu. View only.

settings.name: Exposure mode last registered to a memory slot (P/A/S/M)
settings.note: The exposure mode last registered to a memory slot, not the menu's: a choice in the Shoot Mode carousel leaves it, and a Stills registration in P writes 1, in A 2, in S 3 and in M 4.

settings.name: Exposure mode stored in the memory (P/A/S/M), the value the camera recalls
settings.note: Written when the slot is registered: a Stills registration in P writes 1, in A 2, in S 3 and in M 4.

settings.name: Exposure mode, alternate numbering
settings.note: As 0x10b6, numbered from Intelligent Auto 0, P 2 to M 5; written with it by the mode dial or the Shoot Mode carousel. View only.

settings.name: Drive memory - DRO bracket step
settings.help: How far apart the D-Range Optimizer levels of a DRO bracket's pictures are: Lo or Hi.

settings.name: Drive memory - continuous bracket setting
settings.help: The exposure step and number of pictures of a continuous bracket.

settings.name: Drive memory - continuous shooting speed
settings.help: The burst speed Continuous Shooting uses: Hi+, Hi, Mid or Lo.

settings.name: Drive memory - single bracket setting
settings.help: The exposure step and number of pictures of a single bracket.

settings.name: Drive memory - white balance bracket step
settings.help: How far apart the white balance of a white balance bracket's pictures is: Lo or Hi.

settings.name: Audio Input Master Level
settings.note: Audio Rec Level, 0-31, stored as the level itself.
settings.help: The recording level of the sound: raise it for quiet sound, lower it so loud sound does not distort.

settings.name: Audio Out Timing
settings.help: Whether the headphones get the sound as it comes in (Live) or delayed to match the picture (Lip Sync).

settings.name: Audio Recording
settings.display_rule: With the switch on S&Q the row shows Off whatever is stored (S&Q clips have no audio).
settings.help: Records sound with movies.

settings.name: Wind Noise Reduct.
settings.help: Reduces the low rumble of wind in the sound from the built-in microphone.

settings.name: Interval
settings.help: The time between the pictures of a pixel shift sequence; Shortest is quickest, a longer interval gives a flash time to recharge.

settings.name: Comp RAW Shooting NR
settings.help: Takes several RAW pictures in a row, to be combined on a computer into one picture with less noise.

settings.name: Comp RAW Shooting NR File Compression Type
settings.help: The RAW file type of the pictures taken for composite noise reduction.

settings.name: Comp RAW Shooting NR Number Of Sheets
settings.help: How many pictures are taken to be combined for composite noise reduction; more reduce noise further.

settings.name: Focus Bracket Exposure Lock 1st Img
settings.help: Keeps the exposure of the whole focus bracket at the first picture's, so the brightness stays even.

settings.name: Focus Bracket Interval Until Next Shot
settings.help: The pause between the pictures of a focus bracket, for example to let a flash recharge.

settings.name: Focus Brckt Saving Dest
settings.help: Saves each focus bracket series in the current folder or in a new folder of its own.

settings.name: Hi(E-Shutter)
settings.help: The burst speed Continuous Shooting Hi uses with the electronic shutter.

settings.name: Hi+(E-Shutter)
settings.help: The burst speed Continuous Shooting Hi+ uses with the electronic shutter.

settings.name: Interval Rec AE Tracking Sensitivity
settings.display_rule: Interval Shooting is not available in Manual Exposure: its rows show their defaults there whatever is stored.
settings.help: How quickly the exposure follows changes in the light between interval pictures: Low gives the smoothest changes.

settings.name: Interval Rec Mode
settings.display_rule: Interval Shooting is not available in Manual Exposure: its rows show their defaults there whatever is stored.
settings.help: Interval shooting: takes pictures by itself at a set interval, for time-lapse series.

settings.name: Interval Rec Number Of Shots
settings.display_rule: Interval Shooting is not available in Manual Exposure: its rows show their defaults there whatever is stored.
settings.help: How many pictures interval shooting takes.

settings.name: Interval Rec Shooting Interval
settings.display_rule: Interval Shooting is not available in Manual Exposure: its rows show their defaults there whatever is stored.
settings.help: The time between interval pictures.

settings.name: Interval Rec Shooting Start Time
settings.display_rule: Interval Shooting is not available in Manual Exposure: its rows show their defaults there whatever is stored.
settings.help: How long after you press the shutter button interval shooting takes its first picture.

settings.name: Interval Rec Shutter Type
settings.display_rule: Interval Shooting is not available in Manual Exposure: its rows show their defaults there whatever is stored.
settings.help: Which shutter interval shooting uses; the electronic one is silent and spares the mechanical shutter.

settings.name: Lo(E-Shutter)
settings.help: The burst speed Continuous Shooting Lo uses with the electronic shutter.

settings.name: Mid(E-Shutter)
settings.help: The burst speed Continuous Shooting Mid uses with the electronic shutter.

settings.name: Pre-Capture
settings.help: Records pictures while the shutter button is half-pressed and keeps the last moments before you press fully, so a sudden action is not missed.

settings.name: Pre-Capture Rec Time
settings.help: How far back before the full press Pre-Capture keeps pictures.

settings.name: Selftimer during Bracket
settings.help: A self-timer delay before a bracket series starts.

settings.name: Shoot Interval Priority
settings.display_rule: Interval Shooting is not available in Manual Exposure: its rows show their defaults there whatever is stored.
settings.help: In P and A, keeps the interval steady when the light is low, by not letting the shutter speed grow longer than the interval allows.

settings.name: File Name Format
settings.help: How movie files are named: standard numbering, your title, or the date with your title.

settings.name: File Number
settings.help: Series carries the file numbering on from the last number, even on a new card; Reset starts it again.

settings.name: File Number
settings.help: Series carries the file numbering on from the last number, even on a new card; Reset starts it again.

settings.name: Folder Name
settings.help: How new folders are named: by number (Standard Form) or by date (Date Form).

settings.name: Color Gamut
settings.help: The colour space used with S-Log3: S-Gamut3.Cine is easier to grade toward cinema standards, S-Gamut3 is the widest.

settings.name: Embed LUT File

settings.name: Base Look
settings.note: Base look of the built-in look ST: fixed at itself (0). Its panel has no Look cell, where C1-C6's starts with one; every camera file holds this number. Numbered as C1-C6's base-look list.
settings.help: The built-in look this one starts from. Only the Custom Looks can change it; each built-in look is its own base.

settings.name: Base Look
settings.note: One of two copies of each look's base look beside the one in use (0x0cbe). Changing a custom look's base look writes only 0x0cbe, in the Stills menu and in Movie mode's alike, so neither copy is Movie's. Camera Settings Reset puts all three back to Sony's base looks (C1-C6: ST, FL, IN, SH, VV2, BW) whatever a file had put in each, so neither copy is what the reset reads. A base-look change in S&Q (Program Auto) and in Time-lapse writes only 0x0cbe too, and so does the look panel's own Reset (C4), which puts the parameters back and keeps the base: no menu action writes either copy. Not a per-mode Creative Look: Different Set for Still/Mv lists no Creative Look on this body (Aperture, Shutter Speed, ISO, Exposure Comp., Metering Mode, White Balance, Picture Profile), and only the base look is kept three times, the eight parameters once each. Recorded by the values the camera writes into it: the reset's Sony base look, and each built-in look's own number, in 0x0cbe's numbering. What the camera uses it for is unknown.
settings.help: The built-in look this one starts from. Only the Custom Looks can change it; each built-in look is its own base.

settings.name: Base Look
settings.note: Base look of the built-in look SE: fixed at itself (9). Its panel has no Look cell, where C1-C6's starts with one; every camera file holds this number. Numbered as C1-C6's base-look list.
settings.help: The built-in look this one starts from. Only the Custom Looks can change it; each built-in look is its own base.

settings.name: Base Look
settings.note: One of two copies of each look's base look beside the one in use (0x0cbe). Changing a custom look's base look writes only 0x0cbe, in the Stills menu and in Movie mode's alike, so neither copy is Movie's. Camera Settings Reset puts all three back to Sony's base looks (C1-C6: ST, FL, IN, SH, VV2, BW) whatever a file had put in each, so neither copy is what the reset reads. A base-look change in S&Q (Program Auto) and in Time-lapse writes only 0x0cbe too, and so does the look panel's own Reset (C4), which puts the parameters back and keeps the base: no menu action writes either copy. Not a per-mode Creative Look: Different Set for Still/Mv lists no Creative Look on this body (Aperture, Shutter Speed, ISO, Exposure Comp., Metering Mode, White Balance, Picture Profile), and only the base look is kept three times, the eight parameters once each. Recorded by the values the camera writes into it: the reset's Sony base look, and each built-in look's own number, in 0x0cbe's numbering. What the camera uses it for is unknown.

settings.name: Base Look
settings.note: Base look of a custom Creative Look (C1-C6). Choosing a base gives the look that base's parameters; the panel's Reset (the trash button, "Reset the current look? All parameters are reset.", Cancel lit) puts the parameters back to the base's and keeps the base. Written the same in Stills, Movie, S&Q and Time-lapse.
settings.help: The built-in look this one starts from. Only the Custom Looks can change it; each built-in look is its own base.

settings.name: Base Look
settings.note: One of two copies of each look's base look beside the one in use (0x0cbe). Changing a custom look's base look writes only 0x0cbe, in the Stills menu and in Movie mode's alike, so neither copy is Movie's. Camera Settings Reset puts all three back to Sony's base looks (C1-C6: ST, FL, IN, SH, VV2, BW) whatever a file had put in each, so neither copy is what the reset reads. A base-look change in S&Q (Program Auto) and in Time-lapse writes only 0x0cbe too, and so does the look panel's own Reset (C4), which puts the parameters back and keeps the base: no menu action writes either copy. Not a per-mode Creative Look: Different Set for Still/Mv lists no Creative Look on this body (Aperture, Shutter Speed, ISO, Exposure Comp., Metering Mode, White Balance, Picture Profile), and only the base look is kept three times, the eight parameters once each. Recorded by the values the camera writes into it: the reset's Sony base look, and each built-in look's own number, in 0x0cbe's numbering. What the camera uses it for is unknown.

settings.help: The kind of subject the camera recognises and focuses on: people, animals, birds, insects, cars and trains, or planes.

settings.name: Right/Left Eye Select

settings.name: Face Eye Frame Display
settings.help: Whether a frame is drawn around the face or eye the camera recognises.

settings.name: Regist. Face Priority
settings.help: Gives focus priority to faces you registered in the camera.

settings.name: Auto Magnifier in MF
settings.help: In manual focus, enlarges the picture as soon as you turn the focus ring, so you can focus precisely.

settings.name: Focus Magnification Time
settings.help: How long the enlarged view for focusing stays on screen: 2 or 5 seconds, or until you leave it.

settings.name: Peaking Display

settings.name: AF Transition Speed
settings.help: In movies, how fast the focus moves when it shifts to another subject: 1 is slowest, 7 fastest.

settings.name: AF Frame Move Amt
settings.note: Sizes the step a press of the multi-selector moves a focus frame: under Standard a press moved Spot M's point 30 in X and 20 in Y, Spot XS's 20 and 20, and Custom 1's box 28 and 19; under Large Spot M's point 60 in X and 38 in Y, Spot XS's 36 and 32, and the box 56 and 38, twice Standard's.
settings.help: How far the focus frame moves with each press of the multi-selector.

settings.name: AF point position X (current)
settings.note: The Spot focus point on the 640 x 480 grid (320, 240 = centre), written only when a memory slot is registered: moving the point on the shooting screen changes no live record. With Focus Area on Spot, a Left press lowered X and an Up press lowered Y (the vertical copies kept theirs). Expand Spot keeps its point in the same records. With Switch V/H AF Area Off, Left and Up presses under Spot S, M, L, XL and XS and under Expand Spot moved all eight point records together, the current X and Y and the level, grip-down and grip-up copies: each press moves the point by a step AF Frame Move Amt sets, the same for Spot S, M, L and XL and Expand Spot and smaller for Spot XS, Left lowering X and Up lowering Y. Under AF Frame Move Amt Standard a press moved Spot M's point 30 in X and 20 in Y and Spot XS's 20 and 20; under Large Spot M's point 60 in X and 38 in Y and Spot XS's 36 and 32. Under Tracking: Spot M and Tracking: Expand Spot the same presses moved the same records the same way: a Tracking area keeps its frame's place in its plain area's records.

settings.name: Network block (holds a Cnct. while Power OFF flag)
settings.note: 160 bytes. Its byte 45 follows Cnct. while Power OFF: 1 On, 0 Off (0x03d7 is the setting itself); the rest is not known.

settings.help: Which of the four audio channels you hear in headphones.

settings.name: Audio Signals
settings.note: Audio Signal(Shooting).
settings.help: Which sounds the camera makes: all of them, all but the shutter sound, only the shutter sound, or none.

settings.name: Audio Signals Start End
settings.note: Audio Signal(Start/End).

settings.name: Audio Signals Volume
settings.note: Audio Signal Volume, 0-5, stored the other way round (5 - the volume): 0 was 5, 5 was 0.
settings.help: How loud the camera's beeps are.

settings.name: USB Connection Mode
settings.note: USB Connection Mode, in the list's order: Sel. When Connect 0, USB Streaming 1, Mass Storage 3, MTP 4, Remote Shooting 5; no option writes 2. MTP is refused ("Connected to Remote Shooting. Cannot be executed.") while Remote Shooting is On, even with no session open; chosen with Remote Shooting Off, it is kept when Remote Shooting is turned On again, while the row reads Sel. When Connect. Refused, or not kept, while a remote session is open.
settings.help: What the camera does when connected to a computer by USB.
option_help: Asks each time you connect.
Works as a webcam, sending its picture and sound.
Shows the cards as drives, to copy files.
Transfers files with the computer's photo tools.
Lets software on the computer control the camera and shoot.

settings.name: USB LUN Setting
settings.note: USB LUN Setting. Refused, or not kept, while a remote session is open.
settings.help: Multi shows each card as a drive of its own; Single shows only one, for computers that cannot handle several.

settings.name: USB Power Supply
settings.note: USB Power Supply. Refused, or not kept, while a remote session is open.
settings.help: Lets the camera take power from the USB cable while it is on.

settings.name: Control For HDMI
settings.help: Lets a TV connected by HDMI control the camera's playback with its own remote.

settings.name: HDMI Resolution Still Play
settings.help: The resolution sent over HDMI when you view stills on a TV.

settings.name: Video Light Mode
settings.note: Video Light Mode; 0x18e4 is written with it.
settings.help: How a video light attached to the camera is switched on and off with it.

settings.name: Video Light Mode
settings.note: A copy of Video Light Mode (0x049e): every choice wrote both.
settings.help: How a video light attached to the camera is switched on and off with it.

settings.name: Auto Pixel Mapping
settings.note: Auto Pixel Mapping (Setup Option): On 0, Off 1; turning it Off asks to confirm, as pixel mapping must then be done by hand.
settings.help: Lets the camera find and correct stuck pixels on the sensor by itself from time to time.

settings.name: Drive Mode Dial
settings.help: Whether the drive mode follows its dial on the body (Set with Dial) or is chosen in the menu (Set with Menu).

settings.name: Enlarge Screen Setting
settings.note: Enlarge Screen. Setting it On also assigns Enlarge Menu Scrn to Custom Button 2 (0x0410 and 0x042a, 2547) and puts the monitor on Monitor(Manual) (0x047a 7).
settings.help: Lets you enlarge menu screens to read them more easily; turning it on assigns that to Custom Button 2.

settings.name: MENU Long Press to Switch
settings.note: MENU Long Press to Switch: by its name, holding MENU switches the Screen Reader on or off (not tried). On 0, Off 1.

settings.name: Shooting Mode Dial
settings.help: Whether the shooting mode follows its dial on the body (Set with Dial) or is chosen in the menu (Set with Menu).

settings.name: Speed
settings.note: The Screen Reader's speed, fastest first.
settings.help: How fast the Screen Reader speaks.

settings.name: Volume
settings.note: The Screen Reader's Volume, 0-15, stored the other way round (15 - the volume): 0 was 15, 15 was 0.
settings.help: How loud the Screen Reader speaks.

settings.name: Display LUT
settings.help: Shows Log footage through the LUT chosen in Select LUT, so it looks normal on screen; the recording stays Log.

settings.name: 4K Output Set. (HDMI Only)
settings.note: Only selectable when Rec. Media dur HDMI Output = Off (HDMI Only): 60p 10bit 0, 30p 10bit 2, 24p 10bit 4. Odd values (1, 3) are probably the PAL rates 50p/25p; the camera keeps them but the menu cannot select them in NTSC mode.
settings.help: The frame rate and bit depth of the 4K signal sent over HDMI when the camera records nothing to its cards (HDMI only).

settings.name: Movie HDMI Output Audio CH
settings.help: Which two of the four audio channels are sent over HDMI.

settings.name: Movie HDMI Output RAW
settings.note: Greyed even with Log Shooting On and Rec. Media dur HDMI Output On ("This function is currently disabled."): probably needs a RAW recorder on HDMI.

unproved_reason.why: Greyed on this camera without a RAW recorder connected over HDMI: it can be proved with one attached.

settings.help: Sends RAW video over HDMI to an external recorder.

settings.name: Movie HDMI Output Resolution
settings.help: The resolution of the movie signal sent over HDMI to a monitor or recorder.

settings.name: Movie HDMI Output Time Code
settings.help: Adds the time code to the HDMI signal, for an external recorder to use.

settings.name: RAW Output Setting
settings.note: Greyed even with Log Shooting On and Rec. Media dur HDMI Output On ("This function is currently disabled."): probably needs a RAW recorder on HDMI.
settings.display_rule: HDMI RAW output is a movie function: with the switch on stills the row is greyed out and shows '-' whatever is stored.

unproved_reason.why: Greyed on this camera without a RAW recorder connected over HDMI: it can be proved with one attached.

settings.help: The frame rate of the RAW video sent over HDMI.

settings.name: REC Control
settings.display_rule: HDMI RAW output is a movie function: with the switch on stills the row is greyed out and shows '-' whatever is stored.
settings.help: Lets the camera's record button start and stop an external recorder connected by HDMI.

settings.name: Rec. Media dur HDMI Output
settings.help: Whether the camera also records the movie to its own card while sending it over HDMI.

settings.name: Brightness
settings.note: The viewfinder's manual brightness, with Brightness Setup on Manual: -2 is 0, +2 is 4. Its row opens only with the finder in use, which takes the monitor folded in and the eye sensor covered (an eye at the finder). With the HDMI cable in, its row answers "This function is currently disabled."
settings.help: The viewfinder's brightness when it is set by hand.

settings.name: Brightness Setup
settings.note: The viewfinder's Brightness Setup (open with Select Finder/Monitor on VF(Manual)).
settings.help: Whether the viewfinder sets its brightness by itself (Auto) or uses the level you set (Manual).

settings.name: Dial/Wheel: Separate M mode and other modes
row: Separate M mode and other modes
settings.note: The Dial/Wheel page's checkbox (Custom Key/Dial Set., stills, page 6). Ticking it again copies the M-mode dial functions over the other-mode ones (0x0407-0x040e: dial 2's Other took dial 2's M-mode function).
settings.help: Lets the dials and wheel do different things in M mode than in the other exposure modes.

settings.name: Finder: Histogram
settings.help: Whether the Histogram layout is among those the DISP button steps through on the viewfinder.

settings.name: Finder: Level
settings.help: Whether the Level layout is among those the DISP button steps through on the viewfinder.

settings.name: Finder DISP Mode
settings.note: The finder's display mode in use, the monitor's codes (0x04e5). DISP pressed at the finder steps it through the modes ticked in DISP Set > Finder (0x0cba-0x0cbd), in the list's order, and comes round after one press per mode ticked. DISP Set > Finder moves it when the mode in use leaves the cycle. A settings file sets it.
settings.help: The display layout the viewfinder uses now; DISP steps through the layouts ticked for the viewfinder.

settings.name: Finder: No Disp. Info.
settings.help: Whether the No Disp. Info. layout is among those the DISP button steps through on the viewfinder.

settings.name: Monitor: For viewfinder
settings.help: Whether the For viewfinder layout is among those the DISP button steps through on the monitor.

settings.name: Monitor: Histogram
settings.help: Whether the Histogram layout is among those the DISP button steps through on the monitor.

settings.name: Monitor: Level
settings.help: Whether the Level layout is among those the DISP button steps through on the monitor.

settings.name: Monitor: No Disp. Info.
settings.help: Whether the No Disp. Info. layout is among those the DISP button steps through on the monitor.

settings.name: Monitor: No Disp. Info. exposure display
settings.help: In the monitor's No Disp. Info. layout, whether the exposure information stays shown (On) or hides after a while (TimeOut).

settings.name: Shutter When Pwr OFF
settings.note: Shutter When Pwr OFF (Setup Option; Off brings a warning about the sensor).
settings.help: Closes the shutter when the camera is turned off, to keep dust off the sensor during lens changes.

settings.name: Menu Screen
settings.help: Lets you work menu screens by touch.

settings.name: Operation Area
settings.help: The part of the monitor that works as a touch pad while you use the viewfinder.

settings.name: Operation in Vertical Orientatir
settings.help: Whether the touch pad works while the camera is held upright.

settings.name: Playback Screen
settings.help: Lets you use touch in playback, for example to swipe between pictures.

settings.name: Shooting Screen
settings.help: Lets you use touch on the shooting screen.

settings.name: Swipe Up
settings.help: Whether swiping up on the shooting screen opens the Fn menu.

settings.name: Touch Func. in Shooting
settings.help: What touching the shooting screen does: set the focus point, start tracking, take the picture, set the exposure for that spot, or nothing.

settings.name: Touch Tracking: AE
settings.note: Touch Tracking's AE OFF / AE ON, the carousel's second axis (Touch Func. in Shooting itself is 0x0476).
settings.help: With Touch Tracking, whether a touch also sets the exposure for the touched spot (AE ON).

settings.name: Touch Position Mode
settings.help: With the touch pad, whether a touch puts the focus frame where you touch (Absolute) or moves it from where it is (Relative).

settings.name: DISP Mode
settings.note: The DISP display mode on the monitor: Display All Info 0, No Disp. Info 1, Histogram 2, Level 3 (the SDK's 2-5; For Viewfinder 4 was not offered in Movie mode). A settings file does not restore it.
settings.help: The display layout the monitor uses now; DISP steps through the layouts ticked for the monitor.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: lens name
settings.note: Each slot's lens name; a teleconverter is added to it (the lens's name, then " + 2X Teleconverter"). Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: lens serial number
settings.note: Each slot's lens serial number: a preset recalls only on the very lens it was registered with. A teleconverter leaves it the lens's. Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Priority Key Settings (flag 1)
settings.note: Becomes 1 when PC Remote priority, 2, is set over the SDK; setting camera priority, 1, again, or reconnecting, leaves it 1, and an upload puts 0 back.

unproved_reason.why: A flag the camera turns on the first time PC Remote priority is chosen over a remote connection, and keeps when the camera's priority is chosen again: no menu row writes it.

settings.name: Priority Key Settings (flag 2)
settings.note: As 0x13d2, with it.

unproved_reason.why: A flag the camera turns on with the one beside it, the first time PC Remote priority is chosen over a remote connection: no menu row writes it.

settings.name: Unknown (moves with connection screens; the SDK lists it as Priority Key Settings)
settings.note: Setting PriorityKeySettings over the SDK leaves it; opening Cnct. while Power OFF's Creators' App screen or Bluetooth Rmt Ctrl's Pairing screen moves it.

unproved_reason.why: A working value the camera keeps: it moved when the connection screens were opened, never with a menu choice.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: focus position (probable)
settings.note: Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: zoom position (probable)
settings.note: No zoom position registered reads 65536000 or -1, by the lens. Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: lens data C
settings.note: Written on registering; its meaning is not known. Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: lens data D
settings.note: Written on registering, as 0x168e; an APS-C or A-mount lens might tell what it holds. Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: focal length (mm)
settings.note: The focal length when the preset was registered, a teleconverter included. Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Preset Focus/Zoom: focal length x 10
settings.note: 0x1694 in tenths of a millimetre. Preset Focus/Zoom's six slots: 1-5 registered by a custom key held down, 6 by a lens Function Ring. Mounting a lens or loading a file writes nothing here.

settings.name: Custom box position in use: X
settings.note: The X of the Custom box in use, whichever of the three, as 0x019c is the spot's. Written when a memory slot is registered: moving the box on the shooting screen changes no live record. With Switch V/H AF Area Off, Left and Up presses under each Custom box lower its X and Y records and the two the boxes share, the records moving with the presses, and leave the spot's point records as they are. Under AF Frame Move Amt Standard a press moved Custom 1's box 28 in X and 19 in Y, and under Large 56 in X and 38 in Y, twice Standard's both ways. Under Tracking: Custom 1 the same presses moved Custom 1's records and the shared two the same way: a Tracking area keeps its box's place in the plain box's records.

With Switch V/H AF Area Off, Left and Up presses under each Custom box lower its X and Y records and the two the boxes share, the records moving with the presses, and leave the spot's point records as they are. Under AF Frame Move Amt Standard a press moved Custom 1's box 28 in X and 19 in Y, and under Large 56 in X and 38 in Y, twice Standard's both ways. Under Tracking: Custom 1 the same presses moved Custom 1's records and the shared two the same way: a Tracking area keeps its box's place in the plain box's records.

link_records.name: Wired LAN Connect
link_records.message: ⚠ This file turns both Wired LAN Connect and Wi-Fi Connect off. After the restart the camera will be off the network, and the read-back will fail until you switch one of them on at the camera.

link_records.name: Wi-Fi Connect
link_records.message: ⚠ This file turns both Wired LAN Connect and Wi-Fi Connect off. After the restart the camera will be off the network, and the read-back will fail until you switch one of them on at the camera.

link_records.name: Remote Shooting
link_records.message: ⚠ This file turns Remote Shooting off. After the restart the camera will not accept network remote control, and the read-back will fail until you switch Remote Shooting on at the camera.

link_records.name: USB Connection Mode
link_records.message: ⚠ This file sets USB Connection Mode to something other than PC Remote or Sel. When Connect. After the restart the USB link will not work until you change it at the camera.

text.mymenu_excluded_reason: The camera does not allow Playback items in My Menu
text.memories_intro: The camera's mode-dial memories. Each holds a copy of the shooting settings registered into it.
text.save_load_path: MENU > Setup > Reset/Save Settings > Save/Load Settings > Save
connect_network_steps: Unplug any USB cable between the camera and a computer: while one is in, the camera does not answer on the network.
Wired: MENU > Network > Wired LAN > Wired LAN Connect: On. Wi-Fi: MENU > Network > Wi-Fi > Wi-Fi Connect: On, joined to the same network as this computer.
MENU > Network > Cnct./Remote Sht. > Remote Shoot Function: On.

MENU > Network > Network Option > Access Authen. Settings: On, with a user name and password. Enter the same pair once in the desktop app's Connect to the camera; it is kept in a private file on that computer, never in the settings file.
Leave the camera on the shooting screen: it refuses while in playback, in a menu dialog, or with the mode dial on 1, 2 or 3.
text.connect_network_note: Careful: loading a settings file in which Wired LAN Connect or Wi-Fi Connect is Off drops the camera off the network. The editor warns before sending such a file.
connect_usb_steps: MENU > Setup > USB > USB Connection Mode: PC Remote (with Sel. When Connect, choose PC Remote on the camera's screen when the cable goes in). Mass Storage and MTP do not work.
A memory card must be in the camera.
Connect the cable; the camera shows the remote-shooting screen. Quit Image Capture, Photos, Lightroom or anything else that may hold the camera.
Leave the camera on the shooting screen: it refuses while in playback or with the mode dial on 1, 2 or 3.
text.address_hint: MENU > Network > Wired LAN > Display Wired LAN Info., or Wi-Fi > Display Wi-Fi Info.
text.read_failed_usb: Check the camera is on, joined by a cable that carries data, with USB Connection Mode on PC Remote (MENU > Setup > USB), and on the shooting screen, not with the mode dial on 1, 2 or 3. The steps are in Connect to the camera.
text.read_failed_network: Check the camera is on and on the same network as this computer, with Wired LAN Connect or Wi-Fi Connect on, Remote Shoot Function on and Access Authen. Settings set, on the shooting screen (not with the mode dial on 1, 2 or 3), and with no USB cable to a computer: while one is in, the camera does not answer on the network. The steps are in Connect to the camera.
text.volatile_note: Only the {n} load toggle flag(s) differ, which flip on every load: the camera holds what was written.

exposure.title: Exposure (stills)
exposure.mode_note: The live mode is the mode dial's position, which the camera writes on load.
